tools.name: about_kicksmash
tools.description: What Kicksmash is and how to use it: matches, levels, groups, boards, the API and what we ask of assistants. Read this once before acting.

tools.name: get_match
tools.description: A match or tournament by its 4-character code: players with levels, spots left, venue, time, level range, result. Public data only.

tools.name: find_matches
tools.description: Open, organizer-listed matches at a venue (its public board), with spots left and level ranges. Give the venue name; the slug is derived.

tools.name: get_group
tools.description: A crew that plays together: members' first names and count (their levels are for members only, so null here), weekly slot, whether it asks to join, upcoming matches, calendar feed.

tools.name: generate_schedule
tools.description: Rounds of rotating-partner doubles for 4 to 64 players. Exact when the field is in fours (every pair partners once in players−1 rounds), fair sit-outs otherwise. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: find_clubs
tools.description: Padel clubs: booking link and platform, courts, today's free courts (from the club's own calendar feed, or read from its booking platform's public page: freeCourts.source says which, and freeCourts.platform names it), founding status. Every row says `claimed`: true when the club runs the page itself

tools.name: find_series
tools.description: Tournament series: same weekday and time every week, fortnight or month, with the next edition to sign up for and the past podiums. Filter by city, or pass a slug for one series. Players sign up on the edition's match page.

tools.name: find_coaches
tools.description: Padel coaches who listed their page: clubs, lesson length, languages, the rules students book under (cancellation cutoff, free late passes, notice). Filter by city. Prices are the coach's to tell; nothing is paid through Kicksmash.

tools.name: coach_slots
tools.description: Free starts inside a coach's hours for the next days (default 14). Only accepted students can book them: request_coach first.

tools.name: request_coach
tools.description: Ask a coach to accept a person as their student, by first name or personal token. The coach answers with one tap. Keep the returned personalToken private to the student; book_lesson needs it. Ask the person before calling.

tools.name: book_lesson
tools.description: Book one lesson at a free start for an accepted student (their personal token). Draws from their open package when they have one. Confirm the time with the person first.

tools.name: cancel_lesson
tools.description: Cancel a student's lesson under the coach's rules; the outcome says whether it was refunded, covered by a free pass, or counted. Say the rule to the person before cancelling late.

tools.name: create_match
tools.description: Create a padel match (4 players) or an americano tournament for a person. A tournament may keep fixed pairs (fixedPairs: true): two partners play every round together and the table ranks pairs. Returns the share link for the players and the organizer's private links. Give the person all links; keep

tools.name: join_match
tools.description: Put a person into a match by first name (or by their personal token from an earlier call). Handles waitlists and level ranges; when the level is outside the range, the organizer is asked to approve. On a fixed-pairs tournament pass partner (a first name) to sign up as a pair: the answer's partner.in

tools.name: create_api_key
tools.description: Get a free key instantly for roomier limits and webhooks. Shown once. Not needed for reading or for a few writes a day.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_coach" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Ask a coach to accept a person as their student, by first name or personal token. The coach answers with one tap. Keep the returned personalToken private to the…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_group, find_clubs · Private data: request_coach, book_lesson, create_match, join_match, create_api_key · Public sink: create_match.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_group, find_clubs · Private data: request_coach, book_lesson, create_match, join_match, create_api_key · Public sink: create_match

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_group" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "A crew that plays together: members with levels, weekly slot, upcoming matches, calendar feed." → after: "A crew that plays together: members' first names and count (their levels are for members only, so null here), weekly slot, whether it asks to join, upcoming matches, calendar feed."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
